newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurds surprised by U.S. comments on north Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Kurds surprised by U.S. comments on north Iraq.

text.p: The Iraqi Kurdish group in control of north Iraq said on Thursday it was surprised by comments from a senior U.S. official that Washington was not committed to protecting the Kurds from President Saddam Hussein.
"It's surprising, very surprising," Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) Ankara spokesman Faik Nerweyi told Reuters.
Robert Pelletreau, the State Department's top policy-maker on Iraq, said on Wednesday that the Clinton administration has never been committed to defending a Kurdish enclave in north Iraq.

"That has not been the policy of this administration," Pelletreau told the House of Representatives International Relations Committee in response to a question by Democratic Representative Lee Hamilton of Indiana about U.S. protection from Iraqi forces.

The KDP, which conquered the region earlier this month with military help from Baghdad, said Pelletreau's statement did not square with U.S. attempts to shield the safe haven since after the 1991 Gulf War.

"They have been doing so for the last five years. There are inconsistencies here," Nerweyi said. The United States and its allies patrol a no-fly zone over northern Iraq to prevent any attack by Baghdad.
Pelletreau, Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern Affairs, faulted the rival Kurdish groups for giving Saddam the opportunity to interfere in their decades-old disputes.
"We have no commitment to protect them against their own bad judgment if one party invites Saddam Hussein in" to help it against the other," he said.
Iraqi troops helped the KDP, led by Massoud Barzani, take the key Kurdish city of Arbil last month, prompting U.S. missile strikes on Iraqi targets.
Barzani asked Pelletreau for continued U.S. help against Baghdad at a meeting in Ankara last week, despite his cooperation with Saddam.
